entries.headline: Two terrorism-preparedness requirements
entries.explanation: One required a cold-weather response exercise; the other required an assessment of vehicular-terrorism threats.
entries.rationale: Distinct mechanisms: a concrete exercise/assessment pair makes the accepted preparedness finding understandable in one short entry. Its actions are distinct from D.C. rule changes; the identical National Security actions appear only here.

entries.headline: Removing U.S. forces from specified hostilities
entries.explanation: Nine country-specific War Powers resolutions covered hostilities involving Iran, Lebanon and Venezuela; their wording and timing differed.
material_limitations: The countries, wording, dates, and House sessions differ.
This does not establish a position on every military intervention or authorization question.
entries.rationale: Keeps the accepted cross-country War Powers finding together; pairs it with the assistance contrast to avoid implying one position on all foreign involvement.

entries.headline: Overturning two California vehicle-emissions waivers
entries.explanation: The EPA waivers let California apply its own vehicle-emissions standards: the Omnibus Low NOX regulation and Advanced Clean Cars II. The resolutions would overturn those permissions; these votes do not show support for every part of either rule.
material_limitations: The resolutions involved different waiver decisions and emissions standards.
The votes do not show support for every part of the underlying rules.
entries.rationale: Distinct mechanism: two identified permissions can be explained together while retaining both decisions. The broader disapproval synthesis includes these same actions and would add a second layer of generalization.

entries.headline: Replacing or repealing specific D.C. public-safety rules
entries.explanation: The reviewed proposals concerned youth cases, police bargaining and pursuits, pretrial detention, and policing reforms.
entries.rationale: Names the specific objects of the accepted D.C. finding and adds information distinct from preparedness.

entries.headline: College foreign-gift reporting: replacement supported, final package opposed
entries.explanation: She supported an amendment to replace the bill's text with reporting thresholds, searchable disclosures, some exclusions, and fines or compliance plans. She then opposed the broader final H.R. 1048 package, which also restricted contracts. The final vote does not identify which part she opposed.
entries.evidence_label: Based on 2 House votes · 1 legislative episode
material_limitations: The final H.R. 1048 vote applied to the whole package and does not show which provision Foushee opposed.
entries.rationale: Necessary contextual pairing: the supported replacement and opposed final package distinguish two proposals within one episode. Keeping both prevents the package vote from implying opposition to all foreign-gift reporting; neither pattern is represented by this pair.

entries.headline: Security assistance differed by country and proposal
entries.explanation:
Ukraine: Opposed three aid restrictions with different scopes; supported a measure authorizing support for Ukraine. That whole measure also covered other purposes, so the vote does not isolate every provision.

Jordan: Opposed two proposals to cut or restrict assistance, affecting different accounts through different mechanisms.

Taiwan: Opposed removing funding for the Taiwan Security Cooperation Initiative.

Israel: Supported an amendment barring funds in the bill from being used for Israel. The same amendment reduced the Foreign Military Financing account by $3.3 billion.

The Israel and Taiwan amendments are individual choices, not recurring country patterns. These choices do not establish one uniform position on assistance across countries.

Israel: Supported an amendment barring funds in the bill from being used for Israel. The same amendment reduced the Foreign Military Financing account by $3.3 billion.
The Israel and Taiwan amendments are individual choices, not recurring country patterns. These choices do not establish one uniform position on assistance across countries.
material_limitations: The countries, funding accounts, measures, and restriction mechanisms differ.

presentation_limitations.body: The final H.R. 1048 vote applied to the whole package and does not show which provision Foushee opposed.
presentation_limitations.heading: Final H.R. 1048 vote

limitations: H.R. 881 concerned Department of Homeland Security funding for colleges, while H.R. 1069 concerned covered federal education funds for K–12 schools. Neither covered all federal funding.
The bills covered different China-linked relationships and used different waiver rules; H.R. 1069's funding restriction would begin one year after enactment.
accepted_finding.primary_sentence: Foushee opposed H.R. 881, which would generally make colleges with specified ties to named China-linked programs or entities ineligible for Department of Homeland Security funding, and H.R. 1069, which would generally withhold covered federal education funds from K–12 schools with specified Chinese-government-backed partnerships or resources. Both bills included waiver routes, but they covered different sectors, funding streams, and conditions.
accepted_finding.public_title: Opposed two China-linked education funding restrictions
accepted_finding.title: Opposed two China-linked education funding restrictions

eligible_inventory.rationale: Accepted opposition exists in m14d:covered_china_linked_funding_exclusions, but M14F/M14G deliberately retain a directionless display. A directional section would override it. These two funding exclusions are distinct from the selected H.R.1048 episode and necessary context for any broader claim about foreign-influence rules; the card makes no such claim.

limitations: H.R. 2550 concerned federal and Foreign Service labor-management rules, while H.R. 5408 concerned private-sector collective bargaining under federal labor law.
Preserving existing federal union agreements is different from maintaining employment terms and a duty to bargain during first-contract negotiations.
H.R. 5408 also required mediation and binding arbitration; support for either whole bill does not show which individual provision drove Foushee's vote.
accepted_finding.primary_sentence: Foushee supported H.R. 2550, which would reverse a 2025 executive order that excluded specified federal agencies and units from federal or Foreign Service labor-management rules and preserve covered union agreements already in effect. She also supported H.R. 5408, which would require continued bargaining and unchanged employment terms while workers' representatives and employers negotiated a first contract, with mediation and binding arbitration if talks remained unresolved.
accepted_finding.public_title: Supported keeping collective bargaining in force
accepted_finding.title: Supported keeping collective bargaining in force

eligible_inventory.rationale: Accepted support exists in m14d:continuity_of_collective_bargaining, but M14F/M14G deliberately retain a directionless display. A directional section would override it. This independent federal/private-sector bargaining relationship is not covered by the selected reporting episode and is not an overlap or low-evidence omission.
